This application coming on for admission this day, the   following:
 ORDER

This is the first application filed by the applicant under Section 438 of the Cr.P.C. seeking anticipatory bail in connection with FIR/Crime No.98/2024 dated 27.02.2024 registered at Police Station Kotmar, District Anuppur for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 409 and 120-B of the IPC.
2. The counsel for the applicant submits that the present applicant is being prosecuted for the offences alleged to have been committed by him under the aforesaid Sections.

As per the prosecution, the Purchase Center In-charge, namely, Mr. Chandrashekhar Tiwari, Godown In-charge, namely, Mr. Kirti Kumar Prajapati and the present applicant who is Security Gaurd conniving with each other defalcated 1997.60 quintals of paddy which was value of Rs.43,60,760.80/.

It is contended by the counsel that the present applicant is merely a Security Guard, work of procurement in Vipran Sangh Kotma was with Purchase Center In-charge Mr.

sentences.text: It is further contended by the counsel that the duties of the present applicant are only outside godown and the entire inventory are maintained by Procurement In-charge and Computer Operator.
Unfortunately, the present applicant has been made a scapegoat and the aforesaid case has been registered against the present applicant and Purchase Center In-charge as well as Godown In-charge.
The past criminal antecedents of the applicant is unblemished and he has never been prosecuted for any of the offences.
No custodial interrogation is required in this matter.
If the anticipatory bail is not granted to the applicant, his reputation in the society will be tarnished.
There is no probability of his absconding or tampering with the evidence of prosecution.
Therefore, prays for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant.

3. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/State has opposed the application and submitted that allegation against the present applicant reflect that without verifying the quantity which was mentioned in the Handling Chalan yet the receipts were issued by him regarding quantity of paddy.
4. Heard the rival submissions of both the parties and perused the case diary.

5 . To deal with this allegation, the statement of co-accused Mr. Kirti Kumar Prajapati which has been recorded by the prosecution reflects that on 19.01.2024 District Marketing Officer, Shahdol had verified the stock and upon verification, 97145 bags of paddy was found there.

Later on,
Purchase Officer, on 30.01.2024 stored 124 bags of paddy.
However, Purchase Officer while misleading the present applicant obtained receipts of 102139 bags of paddy.
There is a Panchnama as well on 31.01.2024 and same was signed by the present applicant as well as other co-accused persons also.

There is another order dated 01.12.2023 issued by the Bahuuddeshiya Prathmik Krishi Sahkari Samiti, Kotma is also on record which reflects that co-accused Mr. Chandrashekhar Tiwari was assigned the work of procurement including the quantity of foodgrains.
In the said order itself it is clearly mentioned that in the case of any irregularities, the entire liability will be of Procurement Center In- charge.

6. Considering the totality of the circumstances of the case, the role attributed to the applicant and looking to the order dated 01.12.2023 and also the statement of Mr. Kirti Kumar Prajapati as well as the fact that the applicant is Security Gaurd and his past criminal antecedent is unblemished, this Court deems it appropriate to enlarge the applicant on anticipatory bail, therefore, without commenting on the merit of the case, the application is allowed.

7. It is directed that in the event of arrest, applicant- Ravikant Mishra shall be enlarged on bail on furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/-
(Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer for his appearance before him during the course of investigation or before the trial Court concerned during trial, as the case may be.
